Healthcare providers often do not receive adequate training on proper use and management of metered-dose inhalers (MDIs), leading to improper utilization among patients with asthma. This can result in reduced effectiveness of the treatment, increased risk of complications, and decreased quality of life for individuals living with respiratory conditions.

In addition to providing clear instructions on MDI usage, healthcare providers should also be aware of potential side effects, alternative therapies, and interactions with other medications. This comprehensive education can help ensure that patients receive proper care and minimize the risks associated with MDI use.

Furthermore, healthcare providers' understanding and knowledge about MDIs are influenced by various factors, including patient demographics, provider expertise, and local guidelines. To address this issue, it is essential to integrate MDI education into clinical training programs, promote continuous learning and professional development opportunities for healthcare providers, and encourage peer-to-peer sharing of experiences and best practices.

By addressing these gaps in knowledge and skills, healthcare providers can improve their ability to manage patients with asthma who use MDIs effectively, ultimately leading to better health outcomes and improved patient quality of life.
